title: 任天堂在新财报中对内存供应充满信心

Nintendo 'confident' in memory supply in new financial report
Business
Console
News
Nintendo confident in memory supply in new financial report
As part of the company's quarterly financial report, company president Shuntaro Furukawa affirmed that Nintendo is not suffering due to the ongoing memory crisis, and is confident it has enough supply.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
November 5, 2026
schedule
3 Min Read
via Nintendo
Despite rising memory costs worldwide, Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa stresses that the company is in a position to secure sufficient quantities for its Switch hardware. Said during a quarterly financial report
captured by Reuters
, Furukawa says there has been no major change to the memory situation from Nintendo's point of view, indicating that while the memory crisis is not getting better, it is at least not getting worse for the company.
The worldwide rise in memory component prices has driven
price increases
and
launch uncertainty
across the industry, largely impelled by those components going to data centers. With Furukawa's confidence that the company has a handle on supply for the time being, the Switch 2 price is seemingly not in immediate danger of another price increase, though
Nintendo has warned not to rule it out in the past
. The Switch 2 received a price increase in the United States in September, bumping the per-unit pricetag up from $450 to $500, an increase driven by the price of components like RAM going up.
Related:
Tripwire Interactive expands publishing business to focus on smaller developers and games
This year's price hike may be to blame for a slowdown in Switch 2 hardware sales with a 32.7 percent drop from the previous quarter, though the Switch 2 still remains a higher seller than its Switch predecessor when launch-aligned.
A Bloomberg report
quotes analyst that place the blame for the console unit slump on a lack of major blockbuster titles for Switch 2, as little on the console beyond Nintendo's own
Mario Kart World
has crossed the six-million sold barrier—though, due to the way
Pokemon Pokopia
is split between publishers depending on region, it has likely crossed that threshold in a way Nintendo does not report.
Software sales, meanwhile, did increase significantly overall, with a healthy boost year-over-year for both Switch 2 and Switch 1—the latter benefiting greatly from titles like
Tomodachi Life
and
Rhythm Heaven Groove
. It is also worth noting that the quarterly results were reported the day that
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
was released on the Switch 2 as the company's most notable holiday title. So while the title’s debut aligns with this financial report’s release, any actual monetary impact from
Ocarina
’s launch won’t be visible until the Q3 report in January.
The Switch 2 itself sold 2.67 million units in the last quarter, while the Switch 1 sold 610k, a number certain to decline next year
as Nintendo plans to stop selling the 2017 console in Europe
in February. Despite the price increase and slower sales this past quarter, Switch 2 forecasts remain unchanged, with the company planning for 16 million units overall in the financial year. At the moment, the Switch 2 retains its current superlative of being the fastest-selling console of all time.
Related:
Ubisoft among the bidders for Arkane as Xbox looks to sell the studio
On a milestone note,
Mario Kart 8 Deluxe
—the Switch version of the 2014 Wii U title—has reached 72 million copies sold, marking it as one of the company's most successful titles in their decades-long history.
